correctness.rationale: For every finite marker penalty the renewal loop generating function has a unique positive root; the induced-gap entropy bound H(r)-t<=P E_r[length] follows exactly from D(r||q)>=0, proving both pressure and uniqueness. Superlacunarity gives vanishing lower length sum and exponentially negligible upper tails. Those bounds justify pressure convergence, size bias and exact Palm waiting-time Laplace-transform asymptotics. Only the a_(n-1) mode survives at the microscopic scale, giving geometric(s/(1+s)) jitter, while mean waiting time divided by a_n vanishes, giving the random-phase lattice. The factorial correction is obtained from sum_{j<n}j!/n!=1/n+O(n^-2). The executable finite tests returned 15 root/size-bias tests, 45 Laplace-transform checks and 33 exact renewal-composition identities; these are corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A canonical divergent-ratio return-length class exhibits an explicit qualitative separation between marker-Palm observation and time-stationary observation. For a vanishing fraction of selected gaps to occupy nearly all physical time and produce a randomly translated lattice rather than a Poisson clock is a structural phase distinction. The next smaller length has an independent geometric law, computed with no model-specific constants beyond s; factorial distances additionally admit sharp 1/n corrections. This explains a natural statistical behavior of superlacunary symbolic dynamics and is neither a finite known-table recomputation nor simply a fixed constant substitution.
